findings.title: Accessing `metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly crashes when the integration has no sender
findings.body: The new check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without a fallback. As far as the code shown goes, only integrations created by the installation webhook store `sender`. An integration created another way, such as an older one or one built through `build_integration`, would raise `KeyError` here. That happens when a user re-installs after the OrganizationIntegration was removed but the Integration row stayed, and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. I could not see `build_integration`'s metadata, so I could not confirm which paths store `sender`. Fix: use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and show `error()` when it is missing.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests the 404 path
findings.body: The assertion on "The GitHub installation could not be found." was removed. The new request sends `state=ddd023...`, which does not match the pipeline signature, so the response now comes from the state-mismatch branch in OAuthLoginView. The test passes whether or not a 404 installation is handled, so the 404 path is no longer covered. Fix: run the full flow (init, OAuth callback with the correct state, then `installation_id`) and assert the 'installation could not be found' message again.

findings.title: Network and API failures in the token exchange and user lookup cause a 500
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is called outside the `try`, and `get_user_info` is not wrapped either. A connection error or timeout during the token exchange, or an API error from `/user` (a revoked token or a GitHub outage), raises an exception out of the view. The user gets a 500 instead of the 'Invalid installation request' page, even though the PR says that page is shown when the access token cannot be obtained. Fix: put `safe_urlopen` and `get_user_info` inside `try` blocks and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` when they fail.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL query parameters are not URL-encoded
findings.body: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so `redirect_uri` (a full absolute URL) and the other values go into the query unescaped. A redirect URI that contains `?`, `&` or `#`, for example from a custom URL prefix, would break the query. Fix: build the query with `urlencode({"client_id": ..., "state": ..., "redirect_uri": ...})`.
